item.title: Connecting students to agriculture, one class at a time
item.description:
Connecting students to agriculture, one class at a time jenniferdhogan Tue, 10/13/2026 - 14:22

When Abe Buttimer of Abelaine Farms Inc. in New Glasgow was growing up, nearly everyone he knew had a connection to a farm. 

Today, that connection isn't as common. Many children have never set foot on a farm or had the chance to see firsthand where their food comes from. 

That reality sparked Buttimer's goal of giving every Grade 3 class in PEI the opportunity to experience agriculture firsthand.

As the chair of the PEI Dairy Youth Trust, a local group that supports agricultural education for young people, Buttimer set his plan in motion with help from Agriculture in the Classroom PEI (AITC).

AITC is a non-profit organization that provides curriculum-linked agriculture and food education to students across the province. It started the Grade 3 Open Farm Day Tour in 2015, bringing hundreds of students to Island farms every September.

The first tours in 2015 gave 164 kids the chance to visit four Island farms. Now, in September 2026, more than 1,400 students, representing almost every Grade 3 class in PEI, have visited 34 farms across the Island.

"That was my goal from the start,” said Buttimer “It was a lofty goal in 2015, but it's very possible now.”

The tours give young students a hands-on opportunity to learn about local agriculture, which compliments what they are already learning in subjects like science and social studies.

And for students, the lessons can be as simple as learning where the food on their breakfast table comes from.

When they visit farms like Buttimer's in New Glasgow, students can touch a newborn calf, see where milk comes from, and discover how grains grown in a field can end up in their cereal bowl.

With fewer families having a direct connection to farming than in generations past, helping young people make those connections is important, says Laurie Loane, executive director of Agriculture in the Classroom PEI. 

"I think it's important that our students know where our food is produced, our farmers that are producing it, and that Canada has some of the healthiest, most safety regulated food in the world."

With only one school unable to participate this year, Loane said the reach of this year's tours marks an important milestone for the program.

"Our students absolutely love having the chance to come out and see live animals, see where their milk comes from, be able to go dig potatoes or go see a beef farm... it's just an amazing opportunity for them. And I think the teachers get as much out of the day as the students do."

The farmers opening their doors to students across PEI get something out of the experience, too. For Buttimer, the Grade 3 farm tour day is his favourite day of the year.

"My biggest wish is that they come and experience an actual farm, they see that we're looking after the animals really well, they see that it's not something that you do behind closed doors, it's right here, and it's accessible."

After more than a decade of welcoming students to his farm, Buttimer still loves their enthusiasm.

"They get excited about the littlest things," Buttimer said. "And that excitement drives me."

Agriculture in the Classroom (AITC) works with the Department of Education and Early Years to make sure its programs and resources are curriculum-linked. 

AITC is funded in part by the provincial government through the Department of Agriculture.

item.title: Municipal nomination deadline fast approaching
item.description:
Municipal nomination deadline fast approaching jenniferdhogan Tue, 10/13/2026 - 10:43

Canadian citizens interested in running in the November 2 municipal elections still have time to submit their nomination.

To be eligible, a candidate must:

  • Be a Canadian citizen;
  • Be at least 18 years old on election day; and
  • Have lived in the municipality for at least six months before the election.

Nomination forms must be submitted by the candidate to the municipal election officer or returning officer by 2:00 p.m. on October 16, 2026.

“The decisions made at the municipal level have a direct impact on people’s everyday lives. I encourage anyone who is interested in making an impact in their community to get involved and take part.”

- Minister of Housing and Communities Kent Dollar

Learn more about the municipal elections.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
Ph: 867-767-9140 ext. 11092
Email: charlotte_digness@gov.nt.ca
